---
title: "Correct Bias using Meta Regression"
format: html

## Simulate the population

Let $P(E=1)=0.05$, and require $C=0$ whenever $E=1$. To obtain
$P(C=1)=0.30$ in the whole population, the prevalence of $C$ among people
with $E=0$ must be

$$
P(C=1\mid E=0)
= \frac{P(C=1)}{P(E=0)}
= \frac{0.30}{0.95}
= 0.3157895.
$$

The outcome is generated from

$$
\operatorname{logit}\{P(D=1\mid E,C)\}
= \alpha + \log(4)E + \log(8)C.
$$

Thus, 4 and 8 are conditional odds ratios. The intercept $\alpha$ is chosen
so that the expected population prevalence of $D$ is $7/10{,}000$.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(45)

n <- 1e6

# Target population quantities
p_D <- 7 / 10000
p_E <- 0.05
p_C <- 0.30
OR_E <- 4
OR_C <- 8

# Because C = 0 for all E = 1:
p_C_given_E0 <- p_C / (1 - p_E)
p_C_given_E0

# There are three possible (E, C) strata, with these population weights:
# (0, 0): 0.65; (0, 1): 0.30; (1, 0): 0.05.
mean_D_given_alpha <- function(alpha) {
  (1 - p_E) * (1 - p_C_given_E0) * plogis(alpha) +
    (1 - p_E) * p_C_given_E0 * plogis(alpha + log(OR_C)) +
    p_E * plogis(alpha + log(OR_E))
}

# Calibrate the baseline log odds to the target marginal prevalence of D.
alpha <- uniroot(
  function(a) mean_D_given_alpha(a) - p_D,
  interval = c(-30, 0)
)$root

# Simulate E and then C conditional on E.
E <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = p_E)
C <- integer(n)
C[E == 0] <- rbinom(sum(E == 0), size = 1, prob = p_C_given_E0)

# Simulate D under the logistic model.
p_D_i <- plogis(alpha + log(OR_E) * E + log(OR_C) * C)
D <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = p_D_i)

sim <- data.frame(E, C, D)

# Check the simulated prevalences (they will vary slightly by chance).
c(
  prevalence_D = mean(sim$D),
  prevalence_E = mean(sim$E),
  prevalence_C = mean(sim$C),
  prevalence_C_given_E0 = mean(sim$C[sim$E == 0]),
  prevalence_C_given_E1 = mean(sim$C[sim$E == 1])
)

# The model-implied stratum-specific disease probabilities.
data.frame(
  E = c(0, 0, 1),
  C = c(0, 1, 0),
  prob_D = plogis(alpha + log(OR_E) * c(0, 0, 1) +
                           log(OR_C) * c(0, 1, 0))
)
```

Because the disease is rare, a simulation of one million people will contain
about 700 cases, but the realized number will not generally be exactly 700.

## Simulation study and logistic regression analysis

The following function simulates one population and fits two models. The
adjusted model includes both $E$ and $C$, whereas the unadjusted model includes
only $E$. It uses grouped binomial data for the three possible $(E,C)$ strata.
This gives the same logistic regression estimates as individual-level data but
avoids storing 100 separate data sets of one million rows each.

```{r simulation-study}
simulate_and_analyze <- function(replicate_id, n, alpha, p_E,
                                 p_C_given_E0, OR_E, OR_C) {
  # The only possible strata are (E=0, C=0), (E=0, C=1), and
  # (E=1, C=0), because C is always 0 when E is 1.
  strata <- data.frame(
    E = c(0, 0, 1),
    C = c(0, 1, 0)
  )

  stratum_probabilities <- c(
    (1 - p_E) * (1 - p_C_given_E0),
    (1 - p_E) * p_C_given_E0,
    p_E
  )

  strata$N <- as.vector(rmultinom(1, size = n,
                                  prob = stratum_probabilities))
  strata$Prob_D <- plogis(
    alpha + log(OR_E) * strata$E + log(OR_C) * strata$C
  )
  strata$Cases <- rbinom(nrow(strata), size = strata$N,
                         prob = strata$Prob_D)
  strata$Noncases <- strata$N - strata$Cases

  adjusted_model <- glm(
    cbind(Cases, Noncases) ~ E + C,
    data = strata,
    family = binomial()
  )
  unadjusted_model <- glm(
    cbind(Cases, Noncases) ~ E,
    data = strata,
    family = binomial()
  )

  extract_E_estimate <- function(model, analysis, model_label) {
    coefficient <- unname(coef(model)["E"])

    data.frame(
      Replicate = replicate_id,
      Analysis = analysis,
      Model = model_label,
      Coefficient = coefficient,
      Odds_Ratio = exp(coefficient),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }

  rbind(
    extract_E_estimate(adjusted_model, "Adjusted", "D ~ E + C"),
    extract_E_estimate(unadjusted_model, "Unadjusted", "D ~ E")
  )
}

set.seed(20261016)
n_replicates <- 100

# Save the coefficient and odds ratio from every replicate.
replicate_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    seq_len(n_replicates),
    simulate_and_analyze,
    n = n,
    alpha = alpha,
    p_E = p_E,
    p_C_given_E0 = p_C_given_E0,
    OR_E = OR_E,
    OR_C = OR_C
  )
)

# Calculate the mean coefficient and mean exponentiated coefficient.
mean_results <- aggregate(
  cbind(Coefficient, Odds_Ratio) ~ Analysis + Model,
  data = replicate_results,
  FUN = mean
)
mean_results <- mean_results[match(c("Adjusted", "Unadjusted"),
                                   mean_results$Analysis), ]
row.names(mean_results) <- NULL

knitr::kable(
  mean_results,
  digits = c(NA, NA, 3, 3),
  col.names = c("Analysis", "Model", "Mean coefficient for E",
                "Mean odds ratio for E"),
  caption = paste("Mean logistic regression estimates across",
                  n_replicates, "simulated populations")
)
```
